citation_short: Menges Waller & Gawler. Seed Set and Seed Predation in Pedicularis furbishiae
barrier_or_exclosure: Aluminum-mesh cages over groups of immature scapes; cages removed before flowers opened
timing_relative_to_pollination: PRE-FLOWERING barrier removed before pollination; later predation observed
design: Groups of 3-6 elongating immature scapes under 1.5-m-tall, 2-m2 mesh cages for unrelated spittlebug experiment
quantitative_result: Amblyptilia pica infested 39% of maturable capsules; seed predators reduced mean yield from 25.4 to 2.8 seeds/capsule (N=224, P<0.001); previously caged scapes had same later lepidopteran predation as other plants
pollination_or_development_compatibility: Supports event ordering only: attack can occur after pollination; no post-pollination barrier remained in place
current_use_for_P_rex_G: Supports temporal plausibility of applying a barrier after pollination
notes: Does not estimate barrier effectiveness because cages were removed before flowering.

citation_short: Walsh Arnold & Michaels. Effects of pollination limitation and seed predation on female reproductive success of a deceptive orchid
barrier_or_exclosure: Dialysis tubing secured around every fruit after initial fruit set
timing_relative_to_pollination: Applied 2 weeks after floral dehiscence, after initial fruit set was scored
design: 2011 three-stemmed plants; N=30 in self, outcross and open pollination experiment; all fruits covered after pollination to exclude insect damage
quantitative_result: Final fruit maturation remained measurable: self 0.466±0.08 SE, outcross 0.40±0.08, open 0.10±0.08; seed mass measured in N=29 fruits (outcross/open 0.027 g vs self 0.017 g)
pollination_or_development_compatibility: Fruit-local dialysis barrier was compatible with continued fruit maturation and seed-mass measurement after pollination
current_use_for_P_rex_G: Strong barrier-class/fruit-development compatibility precedent; informs candidate porous tubing/sleeve materials
notes: No contemporaneous unshielded 2011 predator-control; therefore the barrier's causal reduction in predation is not estimable. 2009 unprotected fruit predation was 73% and reduced seed mass by 89%, but year/site differ.

citation_short: Baker-Méio & Marquis. Context-dependent benefits from ant-plant mutualism in three sympatric varieties of Chamaecrista desvauxii
barrier_or_exclosure: Each developing fruit on treated individuals enclosed with mesh bags; control fruits briefly sham-bagged at beginning and bagged again only near ripeness for collection
timing_relative_to_pollination: Bags added as fruits matured after successful pollination
design: Whole-individual factorial exclusion; 24+4 var. brevipes, 24+12 var. modesta, 20+12 var.1 individuals marked in two cohorts
quantitative_result: Seed-predator exclusion significantly reduced sucking and chewing fruit attacks in var.1 (LRT=9.62, P=0.002; LRT=7.07, P=0.008); increased fruit set in var. modesta (LRT=19.7, P<0.001); seed mass showed no treatment differences in any variety (all P>0.12)
pollination_or_development_compatibility: Authors state early reproductive investment and pollination rates were unaffected by exclusion treatments; seed mass also unaffected
current_use_for_P_rex_G: Strong external efficacy/selectivity-class precedent for a post-pollination fruit-local mesh barrier with sham handling
notes: Efficacy was context-dependent and imperfect; some sucking insects attacked through bag holes and some fruits were attacked before they were large enough to bag. Supports pilot design and failure modes, not a portable effect size.

citation_short: Eriksen Molau & Svensson. Reproductive strategies in two arctic Pedicularis species
barrier_or_exclosure: Individual ramets enclosed in white nylon-stocking cages supported by iron thread and a stick from bud stage through crossing experiment
timing_relative_to_pollination: PRE-FLOWERING enclosure retained while natural pollinators were excluded; hand pollination supplied pollen inside cages
design: 1989: 20 ramets from 10 clones caged individually; 1990: 10 ramets from the same 10 clones; 1990/1991 high-altitude cohorts also caged for hand-pollination treatments
quantitative_result: Authors report no seed predation in caged plants. Natural P. lapponica populations had 13.9-37.1% attacked capsules across sampled site-years (Table 4); at Abisko 13-67% of ramets were attacked and 14-37% of maturing seeds were lost in natural populations.
pollination_or_development_compatibility: Barrier demonstrably blocked Pedicularis seed predators while hand pollination still allowed fruit/seed production; natural pollination was not preserved because cages excluded visitors
current_use_for_P_rex_G: Within-genus proof that a physical cage can eliminate seed-predator attack in Pedicularis; informs barrier material/effectiveness plausibility but not selective G under natural pollination
notes: Important efficacy precedent with a major selectivity limitation: pollination was experimentally replaced by hand crosses. It therefore cannot validate a post-pollination P. rex barrier that preserves natural bumblebee access.
